olivia: Heads-up: while validating restore flows I found encrypted snapshot files landing in a bucket path with no tenant tag in our audit index.
rajesh: are they accessible across tenants or just missing metadata?
olivia: at first glance only metadata missing. objects are encrypted with our CMK and KMS logs show grants to svc-restore, but audit-store events are missing tenant_id field.
kai: any change in the restore worker that could strip context? we just merged the RBAC token refresh patch.
olivia: that patch updates ephemeral creds and refresh timing. repro shows sequence: KMS grant -> s3 put -> audit emit; when refresh happened between grant and emit, emit code dropped request-scoped headers.
kms-bot: KMS grant created: grantId=g-89a7 key=arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:111:key/ef12 principal=svc-restore ttl=300 context={"tenant_id":"customer-81","request_id":"r-993"}
olivia: but audit-store entry: {"event":"s3:PutObject","object":"snap-2026-03-25.tgz","principal":"svc-restore","tags":[]} - no tenant_id.
rajesh: that's our gap. audit emitter relies on thread-local context not the KMS context. if creds refresh resets context store, we lose tenant.
ai: (not in thread)
encops: classify this P2 until we confirm no cross-tenant reads.
ops-bot: incident created INC-20260325-077 (severity=P2) assigned to @encops @restore-team
rajesh: quick mitigation suggestions: 1) make audit emitter read tenant from KMS grant context if available 2) make emitter fail/rollback if tenant missing and put succeeded 3) temporarily extend KMS grant ttl to cover refresh window
kai: we can also add assertion in restore worker that ensures tenant tag included before upload completes.
olivia: reproduction steps I used:
1) run restore with tenant_id=customer-81
2) force token refresh mid-operation: export AWS_SHARED_CREDENTIALS_REFRESH=1 && sleep 1s after grant created
3) observe audit-store entry missing tenant_id
rajesh: short-term plan: roll out emitter patch to fallback to KMS context (PR queued), extend grant ttl to 600s in canary, flag uploads without tenant in audit.
encops: verify whether any principals other than svc-restore read those objects. if so, escalate.
olivia: I'll run a scan of S3 prefix for objects in last 72h where audit-store lacks tenant tag and correlate with KMS grant logs; will post CSV.
ops-bot: scheduled job: audit-backfill started (scan id=scan-1739004321)
kai: long-term: rework context propagation to be immutable during operation (don't allow token refresh to mutate tenant binding), and add end-to-end test covering credential rotation.
rajesh: add a migration to tag existing objects in metadata store from KMS grant context where possible.
encops: also confirm cryptographic separation: even if metadata wrong, object keys can't be decrypted without correct KMS grant - check key rotation windows.
olivia: thanks. keeping updates here. if we find cross-tenant decryption evidence, we'll call sec leadership. :lock:
